name: Bentley Speed Six Blue Train 1930
description:
Bentley Speed Six "Blue Train" - Woolf Barnato's chassis HM2855 with the low fastback Sportsman Coupe body by Gurney Nutting and a sideways rear seat. In March 1930 Barnato bet he could drive from Cannes to his London club before Le Train Bleu reached Calais, and won; the coupe became the famous Blue Train Bentley, though its records show it was finished in May 1930 and the race itself was run in his Mulliner saloon. 6.6 litre SOHC 4-valve six, twin SU: 180 bhp at 3,500 rpm; C-type 4-speed (3.364/1.823/1.357/1.0), right-hand change, 3.53 axle; beam axle and live axle on semi-elliptic leaves; 16 in drums with Dewandre servo; 21 in Rudge-Whitworth wire wheels; about 2,150 kg. Right-hand drive.

3D model: "Vehicle 'Blue Train' Bentley" by Anton Sereda - https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/vehicle-blue-train-bentley-dccbd60ca5954cc09040f0554d9212cc, from the re-upload "Blue Train Bentley" by vecarz (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) - https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/blue-train-bentley-wwwvecarzcom-30aa29c6a50d41b19306c4fbd89d8e08
Port, rework, physics, engine sound, gauges, mirrors, lights and skins: Street Corsa Mods - https://streetcorsamods.com/
Klaxon horn: craigsmith (Freesound 438617, CC0).
Driver pose, animations and collider box: Kunos Simulazioni.
